findings.title: RemediationObligation has declared mutable states and a mandatory closure result but no normative legal-edge machine
findings.contract: The normative manifest says the compiler must ingest every legal edge, prose cannot add an edge, every nonterminal row has an outgoing row, and unknown or inferred transitions are forbidden. Section 13 nevertheless declares RemediationObligation status exactly OPEN|IN_PROGRESS|VERIFYING|CLOSED|REVOKED, says the owner may advance it, and makes CLOSED the only release condition for bound resource keys, but supplies no initial-state declaration, transition rows, guards, cancellation/failure/expiry behavior, or terminal predicates for that aggregate.
adversarial_trace: C11 creates the obligation and MAINTENANCE child after a retained-risk disposition resurfaces.
The child completes terminal-clean and the required release/removal and RemediationClosureReceipt exist.
No normative row authorizes OPEN->IN_PROGRESS, IN_PROGRESS->VERIFYING, VERIFYING->CLOSED, or any other obligation transition.

Because prose cannot invent an edge, the compiler must reject the transition or the resource key remains blocked forever; implementing prose-only transitions would violate the single closed-edge authority.
findings.impact: The round-6 repair replaces reopening with an aggregate that cannot be implemented from the normative transition authority. Remediation cannot reliably close, resource admission can deadlock permanently, and REVOKED behavior is undefined.
findings.required_plan_repair: Add a closed RemediationObligation aggregate table to the normative manifest. Define its initial and terminal states; every legal edge and total expiry/revocation/conflict outcome; exact authority/CAS/idempotency guards; child/effect/cleanup bindings; and the single resource-unblock predicate. Align PLAN and generated tests to those exact rows.

findings.title: C11’s mandatory repeat resurface path becomes unusable after the deterministic child or obligation advances
findings.contract: Every trigger, review due, or revocation is required to use C11. C11 performs one atomic absent-or-same CAS across the obligation, link, and child-at-INBOX; only identical canonical bytes replay the original result, while any different payload or idempotency key rejects. Each RemediationResurfaceReceipt binds trigger and observed_at.
adversarial_trace: A first review-due event takes C11 and creates the deterministic obligation/link/child.
The child leaves INBOX or the obligation changes status.
A later revocation, monitor trigger, or next review-due event is required to use C11 and carries a new trigger and/or observed_at.

The existing records are no longer child-at-INBOX/original canonical bytes, while the new receipt is not an identical replay. C11 therefore rejects, and no other legal row records or applies the mandatory later event.
findings.impact: A revocation or later risk signal can be dropped precisely while retained risk persists. The parent and CleanupItem correctly remain immutable, but the replacement obligation cannot receive all events that the contract says must be processed.
findings.required_plan_repair: Separate first materialization from later signaling. Keep one absent-or-same create row for the deterministic obligation/link/child, then add closed CAS rows that append later resurface/review/revocation events to the existing obligation without resetting the child to INBOX. Define same-event replay versus a distinct later event, and require revocation to move or mark the obligation through a legal blocking transition.

residual_uncertainty: No implementation or exhaustive generated-state/model execution was reviewed or required.
Fresh immutable evidence retrieval and human semantic review remain future gates and are not closure defects here.
